chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the apostate, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who turns away from the Religion of Islam and disbelieves in what Allah revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) after his Islam, there is no repentance for him, and his killing is obligated, and his wife is irrevocably divorced from him. Therefore, whatever he leaves should be distributed among his children.'

key_terms.بَانَتِ امْرَأَتُهُ: His wife became irrevocably divorced (divorce of separation)
key_terms.رَغِبَ: Turned away / showed preference for leaving

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for an apostate's marriage, execution, and inheritance in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the definitive ruling on apostasy (riddah) within Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that rejection of the core revelation renders repentance impossible and triggers immediate execution and irrevocable divorce (talaq ba'in). It further clarifies the inheritance mechanics, noting that the apostate's estate passes directly to his children, a nuance that distinguishes Shia practice from some Sunni schools regarding the exclusion of the apostate from inheriting others. The narration underscores the permanence of the marital bond's severance upon the act of apostasy itself, rather than waiting for a judicial confirmation.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’la Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the apostate, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who turns away from the Religion of Al-Islam and rejects what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, after his Islam, so there is no repentance for him, and his killing is Obligated, and his wife is irrevocably divorced from him. Therefore, whatever he has left would be distributed upon his (Muslim) children’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from al-‘ Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about an apostate (one who turns away from Islam).

He (the Imam) said, ‘If one turns away from Islam and rejects what Allah has revealed to Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, after his being a Muslim, his repentance has no effect. (After judicial due process) executing him is obligatory, his wife becomes stranger to him like an irrevocably divorced woman and his assets are distributed among his children.’”
